_comment: Shahnama of Firdausi, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I: Zal and Rudaba romance. Paraphrase passages with notes.

title.en: Zal at the Court of Mihrab of Kabul
title.zh: 扎勒訪喀布爾米赫拉布王庭

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Minuchihr sec. 7

summary.en: Zal rides a royal progress through Kabul, Dunbar, Mai and Ind, and is met with treasure by Mihrab, the wealthy king of Kabul who pays yearly tribute to Sam. Mihrab's praise of Zal — in heart a lion, in strength an elephant; when he is on the throne he scattereth gold, when he is in the fray he scattereth heads — lights a fire in the heart of Rudaba, Mihrab's daughter, whom Zal has never seen.
summary.zh: 扎勒巡行喀布爾、敦巴爾、邁與信德，受到向薩姆納貢的富裕王米赫拉布厚禮相迎。米赫拉布讚扎勒「心為獅、力如象；登座則撒金，臨陣則落首」——此語在未曾謀面的米赫拉布之女魯達貝心中點燃愛火。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: One day Zal set forth on a royal progress with chiefs attached to him in rede and Faith, to view Kabul, Dunbar, Margh, Mai and Ind. At every stage he set him up a throne and called for wine and harp and minstrelsy, and reached Kabul with gladness in his heart.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: There was a certain monarch hight Mihrab, a wealthy and successful potentate, descended from Zahhak, who ruled Kabul but, having not the power to fight with Sam, paid yearly tribute. Hearing that Sam's son had come, he left Kabul at dawn with treasure and steeds and dinars and musk and rubies and brocade of gold, and Zal went to meet and greet him courteously. They came together to the turquoise throne and a table fit for paladins was spread.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Mihrab observed the son of Sam, and said to Sindukht: of all the warrior-paladins of earth not one can tread his steps; he is in heart a lion and in strength an elephant. When he is on the throne he scattereth gold, when he is in the fray he scattereth heads. He hath this one defect: his hair is white. On hearing this Rudaba blushed, with cheeks red as pomegranate-blossoms, while her heart became fulfilled with fire for love of Zal, and passion usurped the place of wisdom.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr secs. 7-8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: The Damsels at the River and the Rosary of Roses

region.zh: 喀布爾河畔（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Minuchihr secs. 8-10

summary.en: Rudaba confides her love to her five Turkman waiting-maids — I am in love, and like a raging sea whose billows surge to heaven — and when they warn her of Zal's white hair and ignoble fostering she flares up: I want not Caesar or Faghfur of Chin; Zal, son of Sam, is tall enough for me. At Farwardin the maids go gathering roses by the river where Zal's tents stand, and the two camps talk of nothing but the other side.
summary.zh: 魯達貝向五名突厥侍女吐露愛情——「我墜入愛河，如浪濤沖天之怒海。」侍女們勸其勿慕白髮之孤兒，她怒斥：「我不求愷撒或中國王；扎勒之子薩姆已足矣。」法爾瓦爾丁月，侍女們至扎勒營旁河邊採薔薇，兩營談論的盡是對岸之人。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Rudaba had five Turkman waiting-maids, five faithful slaves, all girls of prudent minds. To them she said: I am in love, and like a raging sea whose billows surge to heaven; mine ardent heart is full of love for Zal, and in my sleep I cannot tear my thoughts from him. His love possesseth me, heart, mind, and wits; I muse upon his features day and night.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: The slaves thought in amaze and rose at her like so many Ahrimans: wouldst thou clasp upon thy bosom one whose own father hath rejected him, one fostered on a mountain by a fowl? Rudaba heard, her heart flared up like fire before a blast of air, and she shrieked: I want not Caesar or Faghfur of Chin, or any of the princelings of Iran; Zal, son of Sam, is tall enough for me; I do not love his face and hair but him; 'tis for his merits that I seek his love.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: So donning raiment of brocade of Rum, and twisting roses in their hair, they went toward the river-side: 'twas Farwardin, the first month of the year, and Zal's encampment was beside the stream. Zal, spying them from his high throne, inquired who were these flower-worshippers, and one said: the Beauty of Kabulistan hath sent forth from the palace of bright-souled Mihrab her waiting-maidens to the rosary. Zal's heart beat fast, and being love-distraught he walked beside the stream with a single slave.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 9 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

region.zh: 米赫拉布王宮（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Minuchihr sec. 11

summary.en: At dusk a damsel tells Zal all is prepared. Rudaba from the roof cries: thou art well come; and when Zal asks why she should be on the roof and he below, she doffs her scarlet wimple and looses her tresses over the battlements till they reach the ground: seize these black tresses which hang down beside me, all dedicate to thee. Zal will not wound her heart with his hand; he takes a lasso from his servant instead, and hand clasped in hand the two descend intoxicate with love.
summary.zh: 黃昏時侍女告知扎勒一切已備。魯達貝在屋頂喊道：「君至矣！」扎勒問為何她居高而他居低；她便褪下猩紅頭巾，將長髮垂下牆頭直至地面：「抓住這為你而留的黑髮吧！」扎勒不忍以手攀其心，改用僕人的繩索登牆；二人攜手，沉醉愛河而下。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: At dusk they locked the gate and took the key, and then a damsel went to Zal and said: all is prepared, so come. Thereat the chief, all wooer-like, set out toward the palace. Meanwhile black-eyed and rosy-cheeked Rudaba went to the roof, and, when the son of Sam appeared, that high-born maid unlocked her coral lips and cried to him: thou art well come, O youth of noble birth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Oh find some means to let me look on thee, said Zal, for why shouldst thou be on the roof and I below? The fairy-faced one heard the chieftain's words and doffed her scarlet wimple instantly; then from her lofty cypress-form she loosed a lasso, such as none could plait, of musk. She loosed her tresses o'er the battlements, and when they straightened out they reached the ground.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Now speed thee quickly, spake Rudaba from the wall above, and seize these black tresses which hang down beside me, all dedicate to thee. Zal gazed on her in marvel and said: this is not well; may no sun shine when I shall lay a wanton hand upon my Life. He took a lasso from his servant, coiled and lightly flung it; the noose caught and he mounted. She clasped his hand, and both intoxicate with love descended hand clasped in hand to her pavilion, a Paradise adorned.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: The Shah will ne'er consent, and Sam will wring his hands and storm, said Zal, but still by God I swear that I will never break my troth to thee. Rudaba answered: I too swear by Him, the God of Faith and right, that none but Zal shall be my lord; the Maker is my witness. Their love waxed ever as the moments sped, for wisdom was afar and passion near; then from aloft Zal dropped his lasso and descending straight went from the palace of his lovely mate.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: Sindukht Finds the Go-Between and the Ring
title.zh: 辛杜赫特識破傳信婦人

region.zh: 米赫拉布王宮（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Minuchihr sec. 15

summary.en: A dame of honied speech bears the lovers' greetings to and fro, and Sindukht, Rudaba's mother, suspects the visitor who passes in and out. Unmasking the go-between as a pretended cloth-seller, she searches her sleeves, finds Rudaba's ring and costly stuffs, and hales the woman by the tresses; then she questions her daughter, who confesses: one hair of his is worth the world to me. Sindukht, wroth but wise, releases the woman with a charge of silence and weeps over a love that will not listen to advice from any.
summary.zh: 口蜜之婦為戀人傳書，辛杜赫特（魯達貝之母）起疑盤問。識破其布販偽裝，搜其袖中，發現女兒的戒指與貴重布料，遂揪其髮髮而怒。質問女兒，魯達貝坦承：「他一根頭髮勝過全世界。」辛杜赫特又怒又智，令婦人守口如瓶，自己卻為不聽勸的愛情垂淚。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: A dame of honied speech was go-between and bore the lovers' greetings to and fro. Sindukht observed the woman in the hall and cried: whence art thou? Speak! Thou passest in and out from time to time without regard to me. Wilt thou not say if thou art string or bow? With face like sandarac she kissed the ground and answered that she was a needy woman who got her living selling clothes and jewelry to gentlefolk.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Show me the purchase-money, said Sindukht, and set my heart at rest. The woman answered that the moon-faced lady would pay to-morrow. Perceiving that she lied, Sindukht used force, searched up her sleeves and found her knavery: discovering Rudaba's ring and costly stuffs she was very wroth, and catching the woman by the tresses flung her down upon her face and haled her in shameful plight along the ground.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Then to Rudaba she cried: why choosest thou the ditch and not the throne? Tell mother all thy secrets. Love hunteth down my soul, said Rudaba, hanging her head in overwhelming shame; the chieftain of Zabul is at Kabul, and love of him so fireth me that I weep and only live to see his face. One hair of his is worth the world to me. Know too that he hath seen and sat beside me, and that we hand in hand have plighted troth.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Sindukht was lost in wonder, glad that Zal should wed Rudaba, but said: this is no trifle; the Shah will be displeased and send the dust up sunward from Kabul. Then, to make it seem that she had been mistaken, she released the woman and made much of her: act ever thus, discreet and clever dame; now hide this in the dust. And she laid her down in tears and in chagrin, for she saw her daughter's secret bent was such that she would listen to advice from none.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 15 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: Mihrab Draws His Sword, Sindukht Restrains Him
title.zh: 米赫拉布拔劍，辛杜赫特勸阻

region.zh: 米赫拉布王宮（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Minuchihr sec. 16

summary.en: Mihrab returns to find Sindukht pale and distressed; she tells him the son of Sam hath striven to snare Rudaba, and he springs up, seizes his sword, and bellowed like a maddened elephant: her blood shall flow for this. Sindukht clasps him about the waist and argues him down — a better son-in-law than noble Zal there cannot be; by mingling fire with water, air with earth, earth's dark face is made bright — and Mihrab, still vengeful, hears Sam's answer brought and grants his consent, first exacting a promise of his daughter's life.
summary.zh: 米赫拉布歸來見辛杜赫特面色蒼白；她告知「薩姆之子誘惑了魯達貝」。他躍起拔劍，怒吼如狂象：「此女當血流於地！」辛杜赫特攔腰抱住勸解——「沒有比賢良的扎勒更好的女婿；水火相濟，天地生輝。」他終於接受薩姆的答覆允婚，但先要求妻子保證不傷女兒性命。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Mihrab, much gratified by Zal's attentions, returning found Sindukht upon her couch pale and distressed; he asked her wherefore her rosy lips were thus faded. She told him: know that the son of Sam hath striven to snare Rudaba and misled her ardent heart; now 'tis for us to find a remedy.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 16 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Thereat Mihrab sprang up and seized his sword, his cheek grew livid and his body shook with rage; his heart was full, he groaned and cried: her blood shall flow for this. Sindukht sprang too, clasped him about the waist, and cried: now hear thy handmaid speak one word, then do what heart and wisdom counsel thee. He shook her off and bellowed like a maddened elephant: I should have cut her head off at her birth; now she hath wrought on me this devilry.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 16 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: She said: do not speak so wildly. A better son-in-law than noble Zal there cannot be, as all know, great and small; who is there from Ahwaz to Kandahar that wisheth not to be affined to Sam? By mingling fire with water, air with earth, earth's dark face is made bright. She brought Sam's answer and said: rejoice, thou hast thy wish. Mihrab bade her rouse and bring Rudaba; Sindukht, in terror lest that lion-man should lay her daughter dead upon the dust, replied: first promise to restore her to me unscathed, and that Kabulistan shall still possess this Rosary like Paradise. The chieftain promised.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 16 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: The Stars Promise an Elephant-Bodied Son

region.zh: 卡爾加薩爾之地（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Minuchihr sec. 14

summary.en: Sam reads Zal's letter while hunting, pales, and asks the astrologers how fire and water, such opposed elements, can combine; such surely will be the warfare of Zahhak and Faridun. They search the day and return with smiles: the daughter of Mihrab and Zal will be a glorious pair, whose son will prove a mighty Elephant, who shall make the earth clean with his massive mace; through him Turan shall suffer greater woe, through him Iran shall gain unbounded weal. Sam, pledged by his old oath at Alburz, quits the field for Iran to ascertain the Shah's commands.
summary.zh: 薩姆行獵時讀扎勒來信而失色，問占星家：「火與水，如此相剋之元素如何相融？」術士們搜查終日，笑而歸：「米赫拉布之女與扎勒將成榮耀一對，其子將如巨象，以巨錘清世；因他圖蘭將受大苦，伊朗將得大福。」薩姆因昔日阿爾布茲之誓，離開戰場赴伊朗請示王命。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Sam undid and read the letter while coming from the mountains, paled and halted in wonder. He pondered long and deeply and said: if I shall say this is not well, both God and man will blame my breach of faith; if I say thy desire is good, what will their offspring be, this nursling of the fowl and that div's child? Sam when he woke asked the astrologers: how will this end, for these two elements, like fire and water, are opposed completely? Such surely on the Judgment Day will be the warfare of Zahhak and Faridun.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: They spent the day in searching, and then came to Sam with smiles, for opposites combined in his behalf, and an astrologer said: we bring good news about the daughter of Mihrab and Zal, for they will be a glorious pair, whose son will prove a mighty Elephant, who will gird his loins with valour, overcome the world, spare no Sagsars, spare not Mazandaran, but make the earth clean with his massive mace.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Through him Turan shall suffer greater woe, through him Iran shall gain unbounded weal, through him the aching head shall rest, and he shall shut the door of war, the path of mischief; while Rum, Ind, and the country of Iran shall grave his name on their signets. Sam gave ear and smiled. He called the messenger and said: speak gently unto Zal and say: thy wish hath nothing in its favour, but since I have pledged my word I must not seek a pretext for breaking it; lo, I shall quit the field to-morrow for Iran to ascertain the Shah's commands.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Minuchihr sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
